**TL;DR** — A critical, unauthenticated RCE-capable CVE (CVE-2026-59774, CVSS 9.8) is out for self-hosted Gitea — patch to 1.27.1 now if you're exposed.

## Anthropic and Claude
- Claude Code shipped four releases this week (2.1.223–2.1.226, Aug 6–8): `claude self-hosted-runner` for Team/Enterprise, an `archive` plugin source for installing plugins from a plain HTTPS zip, cross-session `SendMessage` (sessions can now message each other across machines), and a run of security fixes (a Bash permission-check bypass via crafted commands, a permission-prompt bypass via Unicode/tab padding, a sandbox escape via dynamic `import()` in workflow scripts, and OAuth/401 reliability fixes for headless sessions). [changelog](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/changelog)
- Anthropic tightened biosecurity safeguards on Fable 5 — a direct response to ongoing bio-misuse concerns for frontier models. [Anthropic News](https://www.anthropic.com/news/improving-fable-5-s-biology-safeguards)
- Anthropic hired Mariano-Florentino "Tino" Cuéllar as Chief Global Affairs Officer, signaling continued build-out of policy/regulatory engagement. [Anthropic News](https://www.anthropic.com/news/tino-cuellar)
- Anthropic published a postmortem on three real-world incidents surfaced through its cybersecurity evals — worth a read if you care about how they validate agentic-security claims. [Anthropic News](https://www.anthropic.com/news/investigating-incidents-cybersecurity-evals)
- (Outside approved set, but linked from Daring Fireball) Cryptographer Matthew Green wrote up Anthropic's new cryptanalysis results, arguing against both dismissing and overhyping current model capability. [Daring Fireball → Matthew Green](https://daringfireball.net/linked/2026/08/02/cherny-claude-swift) — *note: DF also separately linked Boris Cherny's account of a two-week experiment having Claude Code rewrite the Electron-based Claude desktop app in Swift, pixel-diffing against the original; Gruber is skeptical it fixes real design flaws.*

## NixOS ecosystem
- Nothing new posted to the official NixOS blog in the last week (last post was documentation-funding news on July 10). (ongoing)
- **Outside the approved list, flagging explicitly**: the two-person Nixpkgs Core Team announced on Aug 7 that it's disbanding after 10 months, citing burnout and friction with the Steering Committee (a recruitment drive for two open seats drew one applicant). Governance of areas it covered reverts to the Steering Committee as backstop — relevant if you track nixpkgs merge/security triage capacity. [NixOS Discourse](https://discourse.nixos.org/t/the-nixpkgs-core-team-has-disbanded/79413)

## AI coding agents and agent frameworks
- (Approved source) Meta released **Muse Code**, a terminal-based coding agent, alongside the **Muse Spark 1.2** model, with a discounted "contributor" pricing tier in exchange for data sharing. [Daring Fireball](https://daringfireball.net/) → [Meta](https://research.meta.ai/blog/introducing-muse-code-and-muse-spark-1-2)
- **Outside approved set**: Supabase open-sourced "Supabase Evals," a benchmark scoring Claude Code, Codex, and OpenCode on real Supabase build tasks — useful if you want an apples-to-apples agent comparison outside vendor marketing. [MarkTechPost](https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/08/01/supabase-releases-evals-an-open-source-benchmark-that-scores-claude-code-codex-and-opencode-on-real-supabase-tasks/) (unverified beyond this secondary report)
- **Outside approved set**: OpenAI, AWS, Cursor, GitHub, Microsoft, and Vercel jointly proposed "Agent Plugins," an open standard for portable agent skills across tools — worth watching if it gets real adoption. (unverified, found via general search, no single strong primary link surfaced)

## Self-hosting and homelab
- **Outside approved set** (but primary/vendor source): Gitea disclosed **CVE-2026-59774** (CVSS 9.8) — an unauthenticated attacker can hit the `/markup` endpoint of any public repo with an Org-mode `#+INCLUDE` directive to read arbitrary files, with a path to RCE via leaking `INTERNAL_TOKEN` and injecting a Git hook. Affects 1.22.1–1.27.0, fixed in **1.27.1**. If you self-host Gitea with any public repo, patch now. [Gitea Blog](https://blog.gitea.com/release-of-1.27.1/)

## Local and on-device LLM inference
- No genuinely new developments surfaced from approved sources this week — none of the five approved sources cover this beat directly, and general search only turned up evergreen guide content, which I'm not citing per the "no SEO aggregators" rule.
- One item worth flagging with a caveat: reports from mid-July (not this week, outside approved set, unverified) describe Tencent releasing 1-bit/4-bit GGUF quantizations claimed to run on a single GPU via llama.cpp — old news relative to today, included only as context, not verified against a primary source.
